Get encounter rate of predator at size, resolved by food source

Source: R/summary_methods.R
getEncounterByPrey.Rd

Calculates the rate at which a predator of a particular species and size encounters biomass of each prey species, of the resource, and of the other food sources in the model. Summed over food sources this is the encounter rate returned by getEncounter(). Multiplied by \(1-f_i(w)\) it is the diet returned by getDiet(proportion = FALSE), and that is what this function is mainly for: it is how getDiet() and getTrophicLevel() split the encounter rate between food sources.

Usage

getEncounterByPrey(
  params,
  n = initialN(params),
  n_pp = initialNResource(params),
  n_other = initialNOther(params),
  t = 0,
  ...
)

Arguments

params

A MizerParams object.

n

A matrix of species abundances (species x size). Defaults to the initial abundances stored in params.

n_pp

A vector of the resource abundance by size. Defaults to the initial resource abundance stored in params.

n_other

A named list of the abundances of other dynamical components. Defaults to the initial values stored in params.

t

The time at which to evaluate the rates. Defaults to 0. It matters only in a model whose rates depend on time.

...

Passed on to the encounter functions of the components.

Value

An array (predator species x predator size x food source) with the encounter rates in grams per year. Dimnames are "predator", "w" and "prey". The food sources are the prey species, "Resource", "External" and the components that have an encounter rate function, in that order. Unlike getDiet(), the values are not set to zero outside the size range of the predator species.

Details

The rate \(E_{ij}(w)\) at which a predator of species \(i\) and size \(w\) encounters biomass of prey species \(j\) is $$ E_{ij}(w) = \gamma_i(w) \theta_{ij} \int N_j(w_p) \phi_i(w, w_p) w_p dw_p, $$ with the notation of mizerEncounter(), and with \(\theta_{ij}\) replaced by the interaction_resource species parameter for the resource. Further food sources are the external encounter rate, set with setExtEncounter(), and each extra ecosystem component for which you have defined an encounter rate function with setComponent().

Extension hook

getEncounterByPrey() is an S3 generic. Its MizerParams method resolves the standard encounter rate of mizerEncounter(). An extension package that changes the encounter rate with a projectEncounter() method should give this generic a method that makes the same change and calls NextMethod(), so that getDiet() and getTrophicLevel() can split the changed encounter rate between the food sources correctly. Without such a method they find that the resolved rates no longer add up to the encounter rate, scale all of them in proportion, and say so. getTrophicLevel() takes from this method only how much food each prey species and the resource provide. Which prey sizes that food comes from it takes from the predation kernel stored in the model.

This function does not itself check that its result adds up to getEncounter(): the MizerParams method is reached through NextMethod() from extension methods that have already changed the parameters, and the encounter rate calculated from those would include the change twice.

See also

getDiet(), getEncounter()

Other summary functions: getBiomass(), getDiet(), getGrowthCurves(), getMortByCause(), getN(), getSSB(), getSteadyResidual(), getTrophicLevel(), getTrophicLevelBySpecies(), getYield(), getYieldGear()

Examples

by_prey <- getEncounterByPrey(NS_params)
# Summed over food sources this is the encounter rate
all.equal(rowSums(by_prey, dims = 2), unclass(getEncounter(NS_params)),
          check.attributes = FALSE)
#> [1] TRUE
